extracted.intended_audience: postsecondary institutions' Title IX coordinators, administrators, investigators, hearing officers, and campus legal/compliance staff
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for postsecondary institutions on conducting Title IX grievance processes, including investigative reports, evidence inspection, timelines, hearings, and cross-examination safeguards. Focuses on procedures that ensure fairness, notice, opportunity to be heard, and reliable determinations of responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative report must fairly summarize relevant evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The investigative report must fairly summarize relevant evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department does not prescribe specific contents beyond this core purpose; recipients may instruct investigators to include other matters (e.g., procedural steps) but the regulations only require that the report fairly summarize relevant evidence. The decision-maker will separately prepare a written determination regarding responsibility that contains required elements (such as a description of procedural steps taken).

rubrics_metrics.name: Send investigative report to each party and the party's advisor
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must send a copy of the investigative report to each party and the party's advisor, if any, in an electronic format or a hard copy (§106.45(b)(5)(vii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may choose file-sharing platforms that restrict downloading or copying and that still constitute sending an electronic copy; practices or rules that otherwise limit a party's (or advisor's) access to the investigative report violate the provision. A party may request the recipient not send the report to the party's advisor, but default practice is to send it if the party already selected an advisor to avoid burdening the party and shortening review time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide parties opportunity to review investigative report prior to hearing/determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must be given an opportunity to review and respond to the investigative report before a live hearing or other time of determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This review is important to put parties on an equal footing and allow them to identify omitted or improperly omitted evidence. The regulations preserve a ten-day window (and two ten-day timelines in combination) as the practical review period; recipients retain some flexibility to set 'reasonably prompt time frames' for each phase but should not adopt unreasonably short overall timelines (the Department expressed concern about concluding full grievance processes in fewer than 20 days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may consolidate formal complaints arising from same facts or circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient, in the recipient's discretion, may consolidate formal complaints when allegations all arise out of the same facts or circumstances (§106.45(b)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidation is permitted as a matter of recipient discretion to promote efficiency and fairness where complaints are factually linked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practices cannot limit parties' access to investigative report or evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices or rules that limit a party's (or party's advisor's) access to the investigative report or evidence violate §106.45(b)(5)(vii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must send copies to parties/advisors and must not impose internal rules that effectively block access; technical restrictions on copying are acceptable if they still constitute sending an electronic copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection of 'directly related to the allegations' evidence before investigator determines relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must be allowed to inspect and review evidence 'directly related to the allegations'; this universe may be broader than what the investigator ultimately decides is 'relevant.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department finds it beneficial to limit parties' access at the inspection stage to evidence directly related to allegations, with the investigator later determining what of that evidence is 'relevant' for inclusion in the investigative report. This sequencing helps ensure parties see the full set of directly related materials while allowing the investigator to narrow to relevant evidence afterward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may allow submission of additional evidence or written responses
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may give parties the opportunity to provide additional information or context in written responses to the investigative report and may require parties to submit evidence they want the investigator to consider prior to finalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If recipients allow parties to provide additional evidence in response to the investigative report, that additional evidence will not qualify as 'new evidence reasonably available at the time the determination was made' for purposes of an appeal. Recipients may also provide parties an opportunity to respond to evidence the other party proposes after reviewing the report, and may choose whether to provide copies of each party's written response to the other party. Any such rules must apply equally to both parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules and practices must be applied equally to both parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Any rules or practices a recipient adopts (other than those explicitly required by §106.45) must apply equally to both parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure parity in procedures (e.g., extensions, evidence submission rules, hearing decorum) so that neither party is advantaged or disadvantaged by recipient-created practices. Time extensions must account for the recipient's obligation to conclude the entire grievance process within the recipient's designated time frame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-maker must be separate from investigator and independently evaluate evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision-maker must be a person separate from the investigator and must objectively evaluate all relevant evidence (both inculpatory and exculpatory) without giving deference to the investigative report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even though investigators may include findings, conclusions, or recommendations in their reports, the decision-maker's obligation is to reach an independent determination regarding responsibility after considering the evidence and cross-examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live hearings with cross-examination required for postsecondary institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Postsecondary institutions must hold live hearings with cross-examination conducted by party advisors (§106.45(b)(6)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department finds cross-examination a critical truth-seeking tool in high-stakes cases that often turn on witness credibility. This requirement is accompanied by safeguards to limit re-traumatization and promote fairness (see related criteria on advisor-conducted cross-examination, separate rooms, and relevance determinations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-examination must be conducted only by party advisors (parties cannot personally cross-examine)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-examination is only conducted by party advisors and not directly or personally by the parties themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To reduce retraumatization risk, upon any party's request the entire live hearing (including cross-examination) must occur with the parties in separate rooms. The rule contemplates advising/representation by attorneys or non-attorney advisors who conduct the questioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-maker must determine relevance of cross-examination questions before answers
rubrics_metrics.description: Only relevant cross-examination questions must be answered and the decision-maker must determine the relevance of a cross-examination question before a party or witness answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions about a complainant's prior sexual behavior are barred subject to two limited exceptions; a party's medical or psychological records can only be used with the party's voluntary consent. Recipients should oversee the hearing to enforce relevance rulings and prevent abusive questioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may adopt measures to prevent abusive or irrelevant questioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may adopt measures and hearing rules to prevent irrelevant, badgering, or abusive questions and to ensure respectful treatment of parties and witnesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures may include having parties in separate rooms, limiting follow-up questions that are irrelevant, or other decorum rules so long as such measures comply with the regulations and apply equally to both parties. The decision-maker has authority to exclude inappropriate questions by determining relevance prior to an answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties have equal right to cross-examine any witness, including investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations contemplate parties' equal right to cross-examine any witness, which could include an investigator or preparer of an investigative report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.45(b)(1)(ii) grants parties equal opportunity to present witnesses, including fact and expert witnesses. Some commenters requested explicit expansion to expressly give the right to cross-examine investigators; the regulations already permit cross-examination of any witness and decision-makers may observe credibility through such questioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may choose method for calculating 'days' in timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not require a specific method for calculating 'days'; recipients retain flexibility to adopt the method that best works for their operations (calendar days, business days, school days, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients' chosen method should be applied consistently and account for the recipient's designated time frames for concluding each phase of the grievance process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance thoroughness and promptness; 20-day minimum practical concern
rubrics_metrics.description: The grievance process must balance a thorough, fair investigation that permits meaningful participation with the need to conclude a grievance process promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to allow institutions to adopt very short timelines and observed that concluding an entire grievance process in fewer than 20 days has not been widely viewed as reasonable for high-stakes investigations. The Department also withdrew prior expectations (e.g., a 60-calendar-day target) and leaves flexibility for recipients to set 'reasonably prompt time frames' for phases while maintaining fairness.
